people.nehemiah.role: King’s cup bearer who becomes governor of Judah
people.nehemiah.relations: He is the son of Hacaliah and brother of Hanani. He serves Artaxerxes. Sanballat and Tobiah oppose him.
people.nehemiah.meaning: Nehemiah weeps when he hears Jerusalem’s wall is broken. He asks the king to send him, and the wall is finished in fifty-two days. He makes the nobles give back fields taken for debt. Later he returns and throws Tobiah’s goods out of the temple. He shuts the gates on the Sabbath.
people.hanani-nehemiah.role: Brother who brings the news about Jerusalem
people.hanani-nehemiah.relations: Nehemiah calls him his brother. He shares charge of Jerusalem with Hananiah.
people.hanani-nehemiah.meaning: Hanani comes to Susa with men from Judah. They say the wall is broken and the gates are burned. Nehemiah weeps, fasts, and prays. After the wall is built, Nehemiah puts Hanani in charge of Jerusalem.
people.moses.role: Earlier leader whose law the people read
people.moses.relations: The book calls him God’s servant. Ezra reads from the book of his law.
people.moses.meaning: Moses does not act in this book. Nehemiah’s prayer repeats God’s word to him about scattering and gathering. Ezra reads his law to the people. They swear to walk in it.
people.artaxerxes-ezra.relations: Nehemiah is his cup bearer. The queen sits by him in chapter 2.
people.artaxerxes-ezra.meaning: He sees that Nehemiah is sad and asks why. He agrees to send him to Judah. He gives letters and sends army captains and horsemen. In the king’s thirty-second year Nehemiah goes back to him.
people.asaph-forest.relations: He keeps the forest for Artaxerxes. Nehemiah asks the king for a letter to him.
people.asaph-forest.meaning: Nehemiah 2:8 is his only verse. The letter asks him for timber. The timber is for the gates, the city wall, and Nehemiah’s house. Asaph himself does not speak.
people.sanballat.role: Enemy who mocks and threatens the wall builders
people.sanballat.relations: He works with Tobiah and Geshem. A grandson of Eliashib the high priest is his son-in-law.
people.sanballat.meaning: He is grieved when Nehemiah comes. He mocks the builders before the army of Samaria and plans an attack. He asks Nehemiah five times to meet him. Nehemiah will not come. In chapter 13 Nehemiah chases away his son-in-law.
people.tobiah-nehemiah.role: Enemy with friends and family ties in Judah
people.tobiah-nehemiah.relations: He is the son-in-law of Shecaniah. His son Jehohanan marries the daughter of Meshullam.
people.tobiah-nehemiah.meaning: He says a fox could break the builders’ wall. He and Sanballat hire Shemaiah to scare Nehemiah. Nobles of Judah write to him, and he sends letters to frighten Nehemiah. Eliashib later gives him a temple room. Nehemiah throws his goods out.
people.geshem.role: Enemy who asks Nehemiah to a meeting
people.geshem.relations: He acts with Sanballat and Tobiah. Sanballat’s letter calls him Gashmu.
people.geshem.meaning: He joins Sanballat and Tobiah in mocking the builders. He and Sanballat ask Nehemiah to meet in the plain of Ono. Nehemiah says they mean to harm him and will not go. Sanballat’s letter says Gashmu reports that the Jews plan to rebel.
people.eliashib-nehemiah.role: High priest who builds the sheep gate
people.eliashib-nehemiah.relations: He is the father of Joiada. A son of Joiada is son-in-law to Sanballat.
people.eliashib-nehemiah.meaning: Eliashib and his brother priests build the sheep gate and set up its doors. In chapter 13, Eliashib the priest makes a large temple room for Tobiah. Nehemiah calls this evil and empties the room. Nehemiah also chases away Eliashib’s grandson.
people.wall-builders.role: Families, priests, and workers who repair the wall
people.wall-builders.relations: They include priests, goldsmiths, rulers, and men from Jericho, Gibeon, and Mizpah.
people.wall-builders.meaning: Each group repairs its own part, and many work across from their own houses. The nobles of Tekoa will not help. When enemies plan an attack, half hold spears while half work. Each builder wears his sword.
people.shallum-daughters.role: Ruler and his daughters who repair the wall
people.shallum-daughters.relations: Shallum is the son of Hallohesh. He rules half the district of Jerusalem.
people.shallum-daughters.meaning: Nehemiah 3:12 is their only verse. Shallum and his daughters repair a part of the wall. They are the only women the repair list names as workers.
people.meremoth.role: Man who repairs two parts of the wall
people.meremoth.relations: He is the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz.
people.meremoth.meaning: He repairs a part of the wall near the fish gate. Later in the list he repairs a second part. It runs from the door of Eliashib’s house to the end of the house.
people.meshullam-berechiah.role: Builder whose daughter marries Tobiah’s son
people.meshullam-berechiah.relations: He is the son of Berechiah. His daughter is the wife of Jehohanan, Tobiah’s son.
people.meshullam-berechiah.meaning: He repairs two parts of the wall. One is across from his own room. Chapter 6 says his daughter married Tobiah’s son. That tie is one reason many in Judah were sworn to Tobiah.
people.nehemiah-azbuk.role: District ruler who repairs part of the wall
people.nehemiah-azbuk.relations: He is the son of Azbuk. He rules half the district of Beth Zur.
people.nehemiah-azbuk.meaning: Nehemiah 3:16 is his only verse. He repairs the wall across from the tombs of David and on to a pool. He is not Nehemiah the son of Hacaliah.
people.david.role: Earlier king named in places and in worship
people.david.relations: The book calls him the man of God. Solomon is his son.
people.david.meaning: David does not act in this book. Builders repair the wall near his tombs and his city’s stairs. The Levites praise as he commanded. The singers carry his musical instruments at the wall.
people.debt-families.role: Parents and children short of food and land
people.debt-families.relations: They cry out against their brothers the Jews. The nobles and rulers are their lenders.
people.debt-families.meaning: The people and their wives cry out. They have pledged fields, vineyards, and houses to buy grain and pay the king’s tribute. Some sons and daughters are now servants. Nehemiah is angry, and the nobles swear to give everything back.
people.shemaiah-delaiah.role: Man who tells Nehemiah to hide in the temple
people.shemaiah-delaiah.relations: He is the son of Delaiah. Nehemiah says Tobiah and Sanballat hired him.
people.shemaiah-delaiah.meaning: Nehemiah visits his house. Shemaiah says men are coming to kill Nehemiah. He tells him to shut himself inside the temple. Nehemiah will not go in. He sees that God did not send Shemaiah.
people.noadiah-prophetess.role: Prophetess Nehemiah names in a prayer
people.noadiah-prophetess.relations: Nehemiah names her after Tobiah and Sanballat. He adds “the rest of the prophets.”
people.noadiah-prophetess.meaning: Nehemiah 6:14 is her only verse. Nehemiah asks God to remember her among those who tried to frighten him. The book gives none of her words.
people.hananiah-fortress.role: Governor of the fortress put over Jerusalem
people.hananiah-fortress.relations: Our reading text calls him the governor of the fortress. He shares charge of Jerusalem with Hanani.
people.hananiah-fortress.meaning: After the doors are set up, Nehemiah puts him in charge of Jerusalem with Hanani. Nehemiah calls him faithful and says he feared God above many. The two must keep the gates shut until the sun is hot.
people.zerubbabel.role: Earlier leader named in the return lists
people.zerubbabel.relations: He is the son of Shealtiel. The lists name him with Jeshua.
people.zerubbabel.meaning: Zerubbabel does not act in this book. His name stands first in the old list Nehemiah finds. Chapter 12 lists the priests and Levites who came up with him.
people.jeshua-priest.role: Earlier priest named in the return lists
people.jeshua-priest.relations: He is the son of Jozadak and the father of Joiakim. Eliashib is his grandson.
people.jeshua-priest.meaning: Jeshua does not act in this book. The old list names him right after Zerubbabel. Chapter 12 lists the chief priests of his days. It then follows his family down to Jaddua.
people.nebuchadnezzar.role: King of Babylon named in the return list
people.nebuchadnezzar.relations: He is king of Babylon. The list says he carried the people away.
people.nebuchadnezzar.meaning: Nehemiah 7:6 is his only verse. He does not act in this book. The list counts the people who came back from where he carried them.
people.returning-families.role: Families and temple workers in the earlier return list
people.returning-families.relations: They came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua. Nehemiah finds their list.
people.returning-families.meaning: Jerusalem is large, but few people live in it. Nehemiah plans to count the people and finds this older list. It counts 42,360 people by family and town. Some priests could not find their records and were kept from serving.
people.asaph-singer.role: Earlier singer whose sons sing at the temple
people.asaph-singer.relations: Mattaniah, Uzzi, and Zechariah are named among his sons.
people.asaph-singer.meaning: Asaph does not act in this book. The return list counts 148 singers from his family. His sons lead the thanksgiving and blow trumpets at the wall. Chapter 12 looks back to the days of David and Asaph.
people.ezra.relations: The people ask him to bring the book. Nehemiah the governor and the Levites stand with him.
people.ezra.meaning: Ezra stands on a wooden pulpit and reads the law from early morning until midday. The people weep, and he and the leaders tell them not to mourn. The next day they study the law and keep the feast of booths. At the wall, Ezra the scribe walks before one company.
people.law-teachers.role: Levites who help the people understand the reading
people.law-teachers.relations: Chapter 8 names thirteen of them, with Jeshua first. They work beside Ezra and Nehemiah.
people.law-teachers.meaning: They read the law clearly and give the sense. The people understand and weep. The Levites calm them and say the day is holy. In chapter 9, Levites stand on the stairs and lead the long prayer.
people.sherebiah.role: Levite who explains the law and leads the prayer
people.sherebiah.relations: He is listed among the Levites with Jeshua, Bani, and Kadmiel.
people.sherebiah.meaning: He is one of the Levites who help the people understand Ezra’s reading. In chapter 9 he stands on the stairs and cries out to the LORD. He helps call the people to stand and bless God. His name is on the sealed covenant.
people.shabbethai-nehemiah.role: Levite who teaches and has charge of outside work
people.shabbethai-nehemiah.relations: Chapter 8 lists him among the teaching Levites. Chapter 11 names him with Jozabad.
people.shabbethai-nehemiah.meaning: In chapter 8 a Levite named Shabbethai helps the people understand the law. In chapter 11 Shabbethai and Jozabad are chiefs of the Levites. They have charge of the outside business of God’s house.
people.joshua.role: Earlier leader named at the feast of booths
people.joshua.relations: The book calls him the son of Nun.
people.joshua.meaning: Nehemiah 8:17 is his only verse. The people build shelters and live in them for the feast. The verse says Israel had not done so since his days.
people.abraham.role: Father of the people, named in the prayer
people.abraham.relations: The prayer says God chose Abram and named him Abraham.
people.abraham.meaning: Abraham does not act in this book. The prayer says God brought him out of Ur of the Chaldees. God found his heart faithful and promised the land to his offspring. The prayer says God kept that word.
people.sihon.role: Earlier king whose land Israel took
people.sihon.relations: The prayer names him with Og king of Bashan.
people.sihon.meaning: Nehemiah 9:22 is his only verse. The prayer says God gave Israel kingdoms and peoples. Israel took the land of Sihon, the land of the king of Heshbon.
people.og.role: Earlier king of Bashan whose land Israel took
people.og.relations: The prayer names him right after Sihon.
people.og.meaning: Nehemiah 9:22 is his only verse. The prayer says God gave Israel kingdoms and peoples. Israel took the land of Og king of Bashan.
people.covenant-families.role: Men, women, and children who swear to keep God’s law
people.covenant-families.relations: They join their brothers the nobles, who sealed the written covenant.
people.covenant-families.meaning: They take an oath to walk in God’s law. They promise not to marry their children to the peoples of the land. They will not buy on the Sabbath. They will bring wood, first fruits, and tithes to God’s house.
people.jeshua-azaniah.relations: He is the son of Azaniah. He is not the priest Jeshua, the son of Jozadak.
people.jeshua-azaniah.meaning: Nehemiah 10:9 names him first among the Levites who sealed the covenant. The verse says nothing more about him.
people.aaron.role: Earlier priest whose sons serve at the temple
people.aaron.relations: The priests are called his sons or descendants.
people.aaron.meaning: Aaron does not act in this book. The covenant says a priest of his line must be present when Levites take tithes. In chapter 12 the Levites set apart a share for his sons.
people.levi.role: Father of the Levites, named in the covenant
people.levi.relations: The Levites are called his children.
people.levi.meaning: Levi does not act in this book. The covenant says the children of Levi will bring grain, new wine, and oil. They bring them to the temple rooms.
people.city-settlers.role: Households chosen or willing to live in Jerusalem
people.city-settlers.relations: They come from Judah and Benjamin, with priests, Levites, and gatekeepers.
people.city-settlers.meaning: The princes already live in Jerusalem. The rest cast lots, and one family in ten moves into the city. The people bless the men who offer to go. The city had been large with few people in it.
people.solomon.role: Earlier king named in worship rules and a warning
people.solomon.relations: He is David’s son and king of Israel.
people.solomon.meaning: Solomon does not act in this book. The singers and gatekeepers serve as David and Solomon commanded. In chapter 13 Nehemiah says foreign women caused even Solomon to sin. He uses this to warn men who married foreign women.
people.wall-singers.role: Two companies who give thanks on the wall
people.wall-singers.relations: Ezra the scribe goes before one company. Nehemiah follows the other.
people.wall-singers.meaning: The singers gather from the villages around Jerusalem. Nehemiah sets two companies on the wall, and they walk in opposite directions. They meet and stand in God’s house. The joy of Jerusalem is heard far away.
people.balaam.role: Earlier man hired to curse Israel
people.balaam.relations: The Ammonites and Moabites hired him against Israel.
people.balaam.meaning: Nehemiah 13:2 is his only verse. The people read that he was hired to curse Israel. God turned the curse into a blessing. After hearing this, they separate the mixed crowd from Israel.
people.foreign-families-nehemiah.role: Wives and children from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab
people.foreign-families-nehemiah.relatio: They are the wives and children of Jews. None of them is named.
people.foreign-families-nehemiah.meaning: Nehemiah sees Jews who married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. Half their children cannot speak the Jews’ language. He curses the men, strikes some, and makes them swear. The book gives none of the wives’ or children’s words.
places.susa.summary: In chapter 1 Nehemiah is in Susa the palace when Hanani brings news. In chapter 2 he serves the king wine and asks to go to Judah.
places.susa.limits: The marker shows the ancient city’s location. It does not show the palace.
places.jerusalem.summary: Nehemiah and the families repair the wall here in chapters 2 to 6. Ezra reads the law here in chapter 8. Two companies give thanks on the wall in chapter 12.
places.jerusalem.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The gates and wall parts are not placed.
places.jericho.summary: In chapter 3 the men of Jericho build next to Eliashib and the priests. The return list in chapter 7 counts 345 children of Jericho.
places.jericho.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.gibeon.summary: In chapter 3 Melatiah the Gibeonite repairs part of the wall. The men of Gibeon work with him.
places.gibeon.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.mizpah.summary: In chapter 3 men of Mizpah repair the wall. Shallun rules the district of Mizpah and repairs the spring gate. Ezer, the ruler of Mizpah, repairs another part.
places.mizpah.limits: It is not certain which Mizpah this is. The marker shows a possible location in Benjamin.
places.samaria.summary: In chapter 4 Sanballat mocks the Jews before his brothers and the army of Samaria.
places.samaria.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.ashdod.summary: In chapter 4 the Ashdodites join the plan to fight Jerusalem. In chapter 13 Nehemiah sees Jews who married women of Ashdod.
places.ashdod.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.babylon.summary: The return list in chapter 7 names the king of Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar had carried the people away.
places.babylon.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.bethlehem.summary: The return list in chapter 7 counts 188 men of Bethlehem and Netophah.
places.bethlehem.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.bethel.summary: The return list in chapter 7 counts 123 men of Bethel and Ai. In chapter 11 children of Benjamin live at Bethel and its towns.
places.bethel.limits: The marker shows a proposed location for Bethel.
places.egypt.summary: The prayer in chapter 9 says God saw the fathers’ trouble in Egypt. It also recalls the calf they made after leaving.
places.egypt.limits: Egypt is a wide region. The marker shows only its general area.
places.beersheba.summary: In chapter 11 some children of Judah live in Beersheba and its towns. They camp from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom.
places.beersheba.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.lachish.summary: In chapter 11 some children of Judah live in Lachish and its fields.
places.lachish.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.anathoth.summary: In chapter 11 the children of Benjamin live at Anathoth and other towns.
places.anathoth.limits: The marker shows a proposed location for Anathoth.
places.tyre.summary: In chapter 13 men of Tyre live in Jerusalem. They sell fish and other goods on the Sabbath. Nehemiah shuts the gates.
places.tyre.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
sources.web.summary: A complete public-domain reading text for all thirteen chapters.
sources.web.limits: The text gives the account and what its speakers say. It does not prove each event.
sources.atlas.limits: Use the place labels as background. The linked atlas also includes LDS commentary.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: The map points are estimates. A town marker does not prove that an event happened there.
sources.terrain.limits: Modern terrain helps show the land. It does not show ancient shorelines or settlements.
sources.luther-nehemiah.summary: The overview connects the walls, the public law reading, the settling of Jerusalem, and later changes.
sources.luther-nehemiah.limits: This is a scholarly teaching overview. The exact editing dates and the author remain uncertain.
sources.luther-nehemiah-background.summa: The discussion studies how the returning families understand their losses and their shared past.
sources.luther-nehemiah-background.limit: This is a named reading of community identity. Its outline of the history does not prove every scene.
sources.havea-nehemiah.summary: Havea stresses the workers’ choices. He questions the harsh rules about foreign wives.
sources.havea-nehemiah.limits: This is a scholar’s reading with a modern comparison. It does not recover what each wife believed.
sources.mcclellan-nehemiah.summary: McClellan reads the foreign-marriage rule as guarding a community line after the exile.
sources.mcclellan-nehemiah.limits: The timestamp finds the section, not the exact words. This reading does not prove the wives’ beliefs. It is not Church teaching.
sources.throntveit-record.summary: The record names Throntveit’s commentary, its publisher, year, and ISBN.
sources.throntveit-record.limits: The book record was reviewed. The full commentary was not read.
sources.wiki-nehemiah.summary: The opening describes the book and gives a list of sources.
sources.wiki-nehemiah.limits: The opening four paragraphs were reviewed. Disputed history claims are not taken from this page alone.
sources.cfm-nehemiah-2026.summary: The lesson studies work in the face of opposition and help in understanding scripture.
sources.cfm-nehemiah-2026.limits: This source covers selected chapters only. The lesson’s detailed questions about opposition cover chapters 2, 4, and 6.
sources.lds-nehemiah-108.limits: Chapters 7–13 get a brief overview, not detailed treatment. Church application stays separate from historical evidence.
chapters.*.mapNote: The points show named towns and regions. Jerusalem’s gates and wall parts are not placed on the map.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: The map draws no road and no wall line. The book does not give exact paths.
